reference: There is no equivalent GNU command for this loadable's documented primary-superblock-only verifier. e2fsck checks the complete filesystem and cannot serve as a byte/status oracle for intentionally minimal superblock fixtures. Runnable expectations therefore use the loadable's documented subset contracts and an independent Bash encoder for the public ext2 superblock layout and feature bits; no candidate output is used to generate expectations.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and help metadata
Clean ext2 superblock acceptance and verbose field reporting
ext2/ext3/ext4 feature-based classification, including ext4 extents and huge-file flags
64 KiB block-size boundary with matching first-data-block value
Dirty-bit verify-only behavior, -p repair, and -n precedence over -p
Bad magic, short superblock read, invalid free counts, missing image and missing operand statuses
exclusions: Full filesystem traversal of inode tables, bitmaps, directories or journals is outside this loadable's documented scope.
Repair beyond clearing the dirty state bit is outside the documented v1 contract.
Real block-device access needs a disposable VM and a dedicated throwaway device; no device path is used here.

cases.purpose: Confirm fsck is registered as a Bash builtin and its documented help is available without executing a filesystem operation.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t fsck) == builtin ]]
help fsck > help.txt 2>&1
[[ -s help.txt ]]
printf 'fsck builtin and help available\n'

cases.purpose: Accept a deterministic, independently encoded ext2 superblock with sane counts and a clean state; the documented clean case returns status 0. An independent Python byte snapshot verifies the entire image, allowing only the documented two-byte state repair where requested. Captured diagnostics are retained in private files and relayed to stderr.

Check feature-bit classification for ext2, journaled ext3, and ext4 via both extents and huge-file read-only-compatible flags. The fixture encoder writes public ext2 superblock fields independently. Captured diagnostics are retained in private files and relayed to stderr.

Exercise the largest documented block-size encoding (log size 6, 65536 bytes) with the required first-data-block value 0 and verify decoded verbose fields against the independently encoded fixture. Captured diagnostics are retained in private files and relayed to stderr.

Verify that a dirty state returns the documented uncorrected-error status without a repair flag and remains dirty across repeated read-only checks. An independent Python byte snapshot verifies the entire image, allowing only the documented two-byte state repair where requested. Captured diagnostics are retained in private files and relayed to stderr.
cases.stdout: dirty state reported twice without repair

cases.purpose: Check the documented -p dirty-bit repair on a private regular image, then confirm a default read returns status 0, demonstrating that the state was persisted as clean. An independent Python byte snapshot verifies the entire image, allowing only the documented two-byte state repair where requested. Captured diagnostics are retained in private files and relayed to stderr.
cases.stdout: dirty bit repaired and subsequent check is clean

cases.purpose: Confirm the documented -n read-only option takes precedence over -p: the initial and subsequent checks both report the dirty state as status 4. An independent Python byte snapshot verifies the entire image, allowing only the documented two-byte state repair where requested. Captured diagnostics are retained in private files and relayed to stderr.
Check documented status 4 for a bad ext magic and for an image too short to contain the primary 1024-byte superblock. Captured diagnostics are retained in private files and relayed to stderr.
cases.stdout: bad magic and short superblock rejected

cases.purpose: Check that an invalid free-block count remains an uncorrected sanity error even with -p and that the failed repair attempt leaves the image invalid. An independent Python byte snapshot verifies the entire image, allowing only the documented two-byte state repair where requested. Captured diagnostics are retained in private files and relayed to stderr.
Check the documented subset statuses for a missing relative image (operational error 8) and missing operand (usage error 16). Captured diagnostics are retained in private files and relayed to stderr.
cases.stdout: open and usage errors return 8 and 16

cases.purpose: Qualify behavior when IMAGE is an actual block device rather than a private regular-file fixture.
cases.reason: uid 2000 with setgroups([]) cannot open /dev/loop-control or /dev/loopN (root:disk 0660), cannot mknod block nodes (CAP_MKNOD; device nodes are refused inside user namespaces), and the real virtio disk nodes are root:disk 0660, so no block device with known contents is visible to an unprivileged fixture. Reading/writing an exposed loop node needs no capability, so only device provisioning is missing.
